title: A Survey of Parameters Associated with the Quality of Benchmarks in NLP

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying and categorizing 68 generic and specialized language parameters (e.g., lexical overlap, hypothesis-only prediction, sentence length mismatch, N-gram frequencies) to quantify models' reliance on unintended dataset artifacts instead of actual reasoning.
Identifying the occurrence of gender, religious, race, and age-based stereotype n-grams in NLI datasets to determine if they act as contextual biases that predispose models toward specific labels.
Evaluating the correlation between the absence of specific gender information (e.g., using 'person' instead of 'woman') and the prediction of specific classes like non-entailment.
Testing model generalization by ensuring the annotators of the training and test sets are disjoint, evaluating whether models overfit to annotator-specific styles rather than the underlying task.
